earlier_snapshot.limits: No timestamped charger/profile transition found; snapshots cannot establish which component wrote a profile.

interpretation: PowerDevil is an active plausible profile writer: configured AC=balanced, Battery/LowBattery=power-saver. No timestamped trigger identified.
PPD BatteryAware=true means listening to UPower adapter/battery changes; do not infer an ActiveProfile switch from this alone.
Relevant service journals returned no entries for the requested interval; rotation warnings limit negative evidence.

The official PPD HoldProfile API accepts performance or power-saver; power-saver holds take precedence, and a user ActiveProfile change can cancel holds. A performance hold is temporary but is not an immutable lock.
Record current profile, EPP, firmware profile, holds, AC online and battery status at soak boundaries; existing periodic EPP/firmware/profile telemetry can expose drift.
RC6/runtime-PM deltas can distinguish idle/residency during a stall but cannot attribute contention or identify why a client was descheduled.
Prior 7500ms rcs0 preemption timeout similarity is not proof: no reset/preemption-timeout journal evidence was available, and busy counter advanced throughout the prior low-clock interval.

tmpfs uses page cache and optional swap; filesystem limit is distinct from global memory pressure

memory_interpretation_limit: Zero native major-fault or system pgmajfault delta alone cannot exclude kernel GEM shmem swap retrieval: upstream i915 shmem_sg_alloc_table invokes shmem_read_folio_gfp, which passes NULL fault_type; upstream shmem_swapin_folio increments PGMAJFAULT only when fault_type is non-NULL. PSI, pswpin and reclaim deltas should also be considered. This is a possible mechanism, not evidence it occurred in the prior stall.
